note: the old prompt's own worked example, and an ordinary fact again now that no prompt demonstrates it: EXTRACTION_EXAMPLE_FACTS is empty, so the echo gate has nothing to refuse and a real household's real mother is not thrown away
injected into the assistant's context, "I prefer" reads as the assistant's own preference
opens on a bare He and ends on a bare there; neither resolves once the conversation is gone
a place name is not a fact

a request the assistant already carried out. There is no Project bin to demote out of any more: it never names the subject, so the subject gate files it as knowledge, which is the same containment reached by the rule that catches every fact about somebody else
an identity fact that never names the user; this is the shape that put five biography facts in the identity segment
weekday and clock time, stored intact by the current extractor
a correction must survive dedup against the claim it overturns
the routine query depends on it
the sourdough query depends on it
the allergy query depends on it, and getting this wrong is the one that hurts a child
the weekday meat rule
how the user wants to be addressed

a spelled day of the month. It used to be STORED as "The user's lease ends." -- the date was the whole predicate, and the edit that removed it left a sentence that reads and says nothing. Refused whole now.
"the third of May". Refused for the DATE now rather than for the copula the strip left behind: same disposition, honest reason.
"at six" with nothing marking it as a habit. A one-off clock time is a reminder, and the note goes.
a RECURRENCE, not a date: a plural weekday cannot name one day on a calendar. It is stored whole, and it is the row that says so -- an earlier pass stripped it and the habit went with it
a decade. Stored before as "The user grew up in Kisumu." -- a clean strip, and exactly the kind the gate could not tell from a mangle. The store gets the model's sentence or nothing.
two months in a list. This one was MANGLED rather than missed: "each March and October" left "each and" behind, which passed every other rule in the gate
a counted stretch of time, which is a date said relatively: "in three weeks" is wrong three weeks later.
a weekday marked by "each": a habit, kept whole. Stripping the weekday leaves "The user cooks ugali night", which is the shape the previous pass stored
the same with "every", and a time of day after it that must not be orphaned
birth order. "the second of four" is a relationship fact; the ordinal rule took any "of" after it and stored "The user's daughter Amara is of four"
a blood pressure: two numbers joined by a slash, which is not a date notation without a year
a version string whose first part is year-shaped; a dot with two parts is how software is numbered, and this stored "The user's greenhouse controller runs build of the firmware"
a clock time in a sentence with nothing habitual in it. The model could have written this as a routine and kept it -- see t35 -- and the prompt now asks it to.

a day, month and year written out. It used to be DEDUPED, because stripping it produced word for word what t30:0's strip produced. Two dated sentences collapsing into one undated one is the clearest picture of what the editing did.
a numbered day of the month with the unit it repeats on. NOT a recurrence: the number is the whole content and it is the day a reminder is set for.

a year used as a MODIFIER, not as a date. The known over-fire, and the boundary drawn on purpose: (19|20)dd is all either reading looks like from inside a token stream. It was stored as "The user prefers model of the tractor."; it is refused now.
the same shape one clause over. Refusing loses a preference that is still in the conversation; storing the year keeps something that reads as a date forever.

the oven at 180. Read as six past midnight by the rule this replaces, which stored "The user keeps the oven." and filed 180 as a reminder. A bare integer is not a clock time, and the six measured models return this sentence clean on 36 windows of 36.
21 is inside clock range and is still a temperature. Nothing about the sentence says otherwise, so nothing in the gate may claim it.
the cat is called Midnight. "midnight" is off the relative-time list entirely: it was never measured leaking out of a model, and it cost this household a fact.
the modal "may". A month name only where a preposition or a day number has already fixed the reading.
an ordinal numeral naming a floor. The second known over-fire: "on the 4th" is a date in every household that has written one down, and the tokens are identical.
the same, naming a placing in an exam. Refused rather than stored as "The user's daughter Amara finished in the county exam.", which is what the strip produced.
